BRA.note: USDA Coffee: World Markets & Trade (Jun 2025), MY2024/25: production 64.7M 60-kg bags (3,882 kt green) after drought trimmed Arabica; bean exports ~2,655 kt; domestic use ~1,380 kt. World's #1 producer and exporter. 1M bags = 60 kt.

VNM.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: production cut to 29.0M bags (1,740 kt) on drought; bean exports ~1,464 kt, ~95% Robusta. #2 producer/exporter; dominant Robusta supplier to the EU, Japan, Russia.

COL.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: production 12.5M bags (750 kt) Arabica; bean exports ~720 kt, mostly to USA and EU. #3 Arabica exporter.

IDN.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: production ~654 kt, ~80% Robusta from Sumatra/Java; bean exports recovering to ~453 kt. Large domestic consumption.

ETH.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: record production raised to 10.6M bags (636 kt); bean exports up sharply to ~420 kt. Africa's largest producer; high domestic consumption.

HND.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: production ~330 kt washed Arabica; bean exports ~300 kt, almost entirely export-oriented. Largest Central American producer.

UGA.note: USDA Jun 2025: MY2024/25 production ~402 kt (mostly Robusta), bean exports ~378 kt. Coffee = ~20% of forex; ~two-thirds of exports go to Europe (Italy 39%).

IND.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: production ~360 kt, ~70% Robusta; bean exports ~392 kt. Negative net reflects re-export of imported beans for value-added processing plus stock drawdown.

PER.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: production ~258 kt washed Arabica, much organic/certified; bean exports ~240 kt to USA, EU.

GTM.note: USDA Jun 2025, MY2024/25: production ~210 kt high-grown Arabica; bean exports ~192 kt, a top supplier to USA and Japan.

EU.note: USDA Jun 2025: EU green-bean-equiv imports ~2,772 kt, the world's largest coffee market (~2/3 of demand). Top suppliers Brazil, Vietnam, Uganda, Honduras. EUDR rules reshaping sourcing.

USA.note: USDA Jun 2025: US green-bean-equiv imports ~1,404 kt. CY2024 customs: led by Brazil ~454 kt, Colombia ~270 kt, Switzerland ~97 kt (processed re-export). Hawaii/PR tiny domestic crop.

JPN.note: USDA Jun 2025: Japan green imports ~348 kt. CY2024 customs: Brazil ~129 kt, Vietnam ~96 kt, Colombia ~35 kt = 73% of volume. Asia's largest mature import market.

DEU.note: Eurostat/Comtrade 2024: Germany imported ~1,160 kt green coffee — Europe's largest importer and re-export hub (Hamburg/Bremen). Top suppliers Brazil ~489 kt, Vietnam ~182 kt, Honduras ~64 kt, Uganda ~51 kt. ~Half re-exported within the EU.

ITA.note: CBI/Eurostat 2024: Italy imported ~655 kt green coffee, Europe's #2 importer. Brazil ~238 kt, Vietnam ~133 kt, Uganda ~91 kt; ~39% Robusta for espresso blends. Large roasted re-export (Lavazza, Illy).

BEL.note: CBI 2024: Belgium imported ~282 kt green coffee, the Antwerp storage/re-export hub. Brazil ~97 kt largest; Honduras ~28 kt, Peru ~19 kt. Re-exports ~2/3 to France, Netherlands, Spain, Germany.

ESP.note: CBI/Eurostat 2024: Spain green imports ~310 kt; lead supplier Vietnam ~124 kt (Robusta-heavy market) followed by Brazil ~55 kt. Significant Torrefacto/blend roasting.

NLD.note: CBI/Eurostat 2024: Netherlands green imports ~300 kt; top suppliers Brazil, Vietnam and Belgium (re-export). Amsterdam/Rotterdam trading and JDE Peet's roasting hub.

CAN.note: Comtrade 2024: Canada green/roasted imports ~210 kt green-equiv; sources largely Colombia, Brazil and US-processed re-export.

GBR.note: Comtrade 2024: UK green-bean-equiv imports ~250 kt; sources Brazil, Vietnam, Colombia plus EU re-export. Post-Brexit much volume routes via continental hubs.

KOR.note: Comtrade 2024: South Korea green imports ~190 kt, one of the fastest-growing Asian markets; suppliers Brazil, Vietnam, Colombia, Ethiopia.

RUS.note: IndexBox/Comtrade 2024: Russia green imports ~215 kt. Vietnam ~22%, Colombia ~17%, Brazil ~15% by volume; price-sensitive, Robusta-heavy. Some re-export to CIS.

DZA.note: ICO/Comtrade 2024: Algeria imports ~130 kt green coffee, the largest African import market and a major Robusta destination (Vietnam, Ivory Coast, Brazil). Poor Comtrade reporter — leans on mirror data and ICO; treat as indicative.

CHN.note: Comtrade 2024 + USDA: China grows ~132 kt (mostly Yunnan Arabica) but is now a fast-rising net importer (~260 kt green-equiv); suppliers Brazil, Colombia, Ethiopia, Vietnam.

CHE.note: Swiss customs 2024: imported ~216 kt green coffee but is a huge value-added re-exporter — #2 roasted-coffee exporter by value (Nespresso/Nestle capsules). Positive net = processed re-export exceeds domestic use.

rankings.note: Exporter ranking = USDA Coffee: World Markets & Trade (Jun 2025) MY2024/25 green-bean exports (60 kt/M bags). Importer ranking = USDA green-bean-equiv (EU, USA, Japan) plus Eurostat/UN Comtrade 2024 national customs. EU appears as the bloc aggregate AND as member-state importers (Germany, Italy, etc.), which double-count within the EU total. Switzerland's figure is physical green handling; its true role is value-added re-export.

companies.name: Nestle
companies.metric: Group revenue CHF 91.4bn (FY2024); coffee (Nescafe + Nespresso) the largest growth contributor
companies.note: World's largest coffee company by sales (Nescafe, Nespresso, Starbucks at-home license). Buys green coffee globally; runs the Swiss Nespresso capsule factories.
companies.improve: Should publish farm-gate origin volumes by country and EUDR-traceability coverage for Nescafe's high-Robusta supply chains (Vietnam, Indonesia, Uganda).

companies.name: JDE Peet's
companies.note: World's leading pure-play coffee & tea group (Jacobs, Douwe Egberts, L'OR, Peet's). Major green-coffee buyer routed through the Netherlands/Belgium hubs.
companies.improve: Should disclose green-coffee volumes by origin and the Robusta/Arabica split to size EUDR exposure.

companies.name: Starbucks
companies.note: World's largest coffee retailer; buys premium washed Arabica via C.A.F.E. Practices, much sourced by traders like ofi.
companies.improve: Should publish green-coffee tonnage by origin and price floors paid to assess farmer price transmission as ICO prices spiked.

companies.name: Neumann Kaffee Gruppe
companies.metric: ~840 kt handled (~8.5% of world consumption); world's largest green-coffee trader
companies.note: Privately held #1 green-coffee trading and milling group, origin operations across Latin America, Africa, Asia.
companies.improve: Should disclose audited annual handled volume and EUDR-aligned share by origin.

companies.name: ECOM Agroindustrial
companies.metric: ~780+ kt, historically ~7% of world coffee; world's largest coffee miller
companies.note: Privately held soft-commodity trader. Volume figure is a historical disclosure carried forward — current scale comparable or larger but undisclosed.
companies.improve: Should publish current-year handled bags by origin and milling capacity to verify its top-3 trader status.

companies.name: ofi (Olam Food Ingredients)
companies.metric: Top-tier global green-coffee trader & soluble-coffee maker; sources from ~2.8M farmers
companies.note: Olam Group's food-ingredients arm; integrated coffee supplier to Nestle, Starbucks. Coffee-specific bag volumes not separately disclosed.
companies.improve: Should break out coffee green-bean tonnage by origin and report EUDR/deforestation-free coverage for Vietnam/Indonesia Robusta.

companies.name: Lavazza Group
companies.note: Family-owned Italian roaster (Lavazza, Carte Noire, Kicking Horse). Italy-centric buyer of Brazilian Arabica and Vietnamese/Ugandan Robusta.
companies.improve: Should publish green-coffee origin volumes and the certified/EUDR-traceable share given heavy Ugandan and Vietnamese Robusta reliance.

global.note: World coffee totals, kt green-bean-equivalent (1M 60-kg bags = 60 kt), USDA and ICO. Years label the start of the split coffee year (2024 = MY2024/25). MY2024/25 production ~10,464 kt, consumption a record ~10,164 kt, total exports (beans + soluble/roasted) ~8,830 kt; bean-only ~7,290 kt. The 2021/22 dip reflects Brazil frost/drought; ICO composite price rose >90% across 2023-2024.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook envelope; 2030 = 2024×(1+rate)^6. World demand ~+1.5%/yr led by Asia, supply from Brazil Robusta + Vietnam/Indonesia recovery + Ethiopia/Uganda; climate downside on Arabica.
